findings.issue_text: **`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts` (isTeamAdminOrOwner computation)**: `isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` uses `&&` instead of `||`. As written, only a user who is simultaneously flagged admin AND owner passes — a legitimate team admin (not owner) or owner (not flagged admin) is incorrectly denied when they're neither the organizer nor an attendee. The variable name itself signals the intended logic was OR. Fix: `isTeamAdmin(...) || isTeamOwner(...)`.

**No tests added.** A new authorization-guarded mutation (`addGuestsHandler`) with four permission branches (organizer, attendee, team admin, team owner, unauthorized), a dedup/blacklist filter, and an error path with `BAD_REQUEST` has zero test coverage. Given this PR is entirely new backend logic that mutates bookings and sends emails, this should not ship without at least handler-level tests covering: happy path, `booking_not_found`, unauthorized user, duplicate-only guests, and blacklist filtering.

**Calendar sync failure leaves DB/calendar inconsistent.** In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `prisma.booking.update` (guest insert) commits before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs, and the latter is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar sync throws, the mutation errors out to the client, but the new attendees are already persisted in the DB — the booking's guest list and the actual calendar event (and any emails already sent) go out of sync with no rollback or compensating action.

**Blacklist bypass via case.** `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guest` (from user input) is compared as-is: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a blacklist entry of `blocked@example.com`. Same issue for the existing-attendee dedup check (`guest === attendee.email`), which is also case-sensitive — could produce duplicate attendee rows differing only by case.

**Misleading error message conflates two different causes.** `uniqueGuests.length === 0` throws `emails_must_be_unique_valid` whether the guests were already attendees or were blacklisted. A user submitting only blacklisted emails gets a message implying their email format was invalid/duplicated, not that it was blocked.

**Wrong data passed to email branching logic.** `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the original (unfiltered) `guests` array, not `uniqueGuests`. Inside `email-manager.ts`, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` decides whether an attendee is sent `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (as if newly booked) vs. `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If a submitted email matched an existing attendee (filtered out of `uniqueGuests` but still in `guests`), that existing attendee will incorrectly get the "you're newly scheduled" email again.

**Errors from `sendAddGuestsEmails` are swallowed with a bare `console.log`**, no error object/stack, no structured logging. The mutation still returns success to the client even when every notification email failed, giving a false-positive UX signal with no operational visibility.

**Missing translation key.** `you_do_not_have_permission` (thrown as the `TRPCError` message and consumed via `t(err.message)` in the dialog) does not exist in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json`. Users hitting this path will see the raw untranslated key/string instead of a real message.

**No cap on number of guests.** `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.min(1)`/`.max(n)`. A caller (or a buggy client state) could submit an empty array or an unbounded number of emails in one call, causing an unbounded `createMany` insert and an unbounded email fan-out via `Promise.all` in `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

**Credentials used for calendar sync are the requester's, not the organizer's.** `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches the *calling* user's credentials, but the calendar event being updated belongs to the booking's organizer. When a non-organizer attendee (who is permitted via `isAttendee`) calls this mutation, `EventManager` is built with the wrong user's calendar credentials, which will likely no-op or fail silently for the actual calendar update.

`addGuestsHandler` is a single ~150-line function mixing auth, Prisma queries, `CalendarEvent` construction, calendar sync, and email dispatch — worth decomposing for readability/testability, consistent with other patterns in the router.

Client (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx`) re-declares its own Zod validation schema instead of importing `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` from `addGuests.schema.ts`; the two can silently drift (e.g., server schema doesn't currently enforce uniqueness at all).

`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`/`OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` template classes (`packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`) duplicate near-identical `getNodeMailerPayload` bodies from their `*-scheduled-email.ts` counterparts; could share more via the parent class.
`getTranslation` is invoked per-attendee inside `Promise.all` without any caching, so bookings with many attendees/guests incur N sequential-per-item i18n loads.
`isTeamAdmin`/`isTeamOwner` are awaited sequentially rather than via `Promise.all`, adding avoidable latency to every call.
Hardcoded `name: ""` for new guest attendee records — fine for now since the UI only collects emails, but worth a comment noting the limitation for future readers.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Calendar sync failure leaves DB/calendar inconsistent.** In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `prisma.booking.update` (guest insert) commits before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs, and the latter is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar sync throws, the mutation errors out to the client, but the new attendees are already persisted in the DB — the booking's guest list and the actual calendar event (and any emails already sent) go out of sync with no rollback or compensating action.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no transaction and no try/catch around the calendar update. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will error out while the DB has already been modified, leaving DB attendees updated but the external calendar event potentially not updated (no rollback/compensation in the diff). Note: the finding’s mention of “emails already sent” is not accurate here because emails are sent after the calendar update (and in a try/catch), but the DB/calendar inconsistency risk is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Misleading error message conflates two different causes.** `uniqueGuests.length === 0` throws `emails_must_be_unique_valid` whether the guests were already attendees or were blacklisted. A user submitting only blacklisted emails gets a message implying their email format was invalid/duplicated, not that it was blocked.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out (a) emails already present in `booking.attendees` and (b) emails in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. If that filtering removes everything, the code throws `new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`. That message key (added in locales as "Emails must be unique and valid") does not reflect the case where emails are syntactically valid but rejected due to blacklist (or simply already attendees). So the same error is used for multiple distinct causes, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Wrong data passed to email branching logic.** `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the original (unfiltered) `guests` array, not `uniqueGuests`. Inside `email-manager.ts`, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` decides whether an attendee is sent `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (as if newly booked) vs. `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If a submitted email matched an existing attendee (filtered out of `uniqueGuests` but still in `guests`), that existing attendee will incorrectly get the "you're newly scheduled" email again.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code correctly computes `uniqueGuests` (excluding already-existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only adds those to the booking. However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original, unfiltered `guests` array. In `packages/emails/email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide which email template to send per attendee. If the request included an email that already existed on the booking (filtered out of `uniqueGuests` but still present in `guests`), that existing attendee will satisfy the `includes` check and be treated as a “new guest”, receiving `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the intended update email. This is directly verifiable from the diff and is a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Errors from `sendAddGuestsEmails` are swallowed with a bare `console.log`**, no error object/stack, no structured logging. The mutation still returns success to the client even when every notification email failed, giving a false-positive UX signal with no operational visibility.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` which (1) discards the caught `err` so no stack/details are logged, and (2) does not propagate/report the failure, so the mutation proceeds to return `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the client `onSuccess` path shows a success toast even if `sendAddGuestsEmails` fails. This is directly present in the diff and reduces operational visibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Missing translation key.** `you_do_not_have_permission` (thrown as the `TRPCError` message and consumed via `t(err.message)` in the dialog) does not exist in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json`. Users hitting this path will see the raw untranslated key/string instead of a real message.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `addGuests.handler.ts` throwing `new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" })`, and the client dialog renders errors via `t(err.message)`. However, the claim that `you_do_not_have_permission` “does not exist” in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json` is not verifiable from the provided diff: the locale file is only partially shown around unrelated keys, and the key could already exist elsewhere in that same JSON (or another loaded namespace) prior to this change. The diff itself does not remove or rename that key, nor does it definitively show it missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **No cap on number of guests.** `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.min(1)`/`.max(n)`. A caller (or a buggy client state) could submit an empty array or an unbounded number of emails in one call, causing an unbounded `createMany` insert and an unbounded email fan-out via `Promise.all` in `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `addGuests` with input schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` that has no `.max(...)`, and the handler directly uses the resulting list to (a) `createMany` attendees and (b) trigger an email fan-out via `sendAddGuestsEmails` which builds an array of email send promises and `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)`. That makes the request cost proportional to the number of submitted emails and could be abused by an authorized caller (organizer/attendee/team admin/owner) to cause very large DB writes and mass email sends in one call. However, the “empty array” part is less accurate: the handler rejects empty/ineffective input because `uniqueGuests.length === 0` throws `BAD_REQUEST`, so an empty `guests` array won’t succeed even though the schema allows it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Credentials used for calendar sync are the requester's, not the organizer's.** `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches the *calling* user's credentials, but the calendar event being updated belongs to the booking's organizer. When a non-organizer attendee (who is permitted via `isAttendee`) calls this mutation, `EventManager` is built with the wrong user's calendar credentials, which will likely no-op or fail silently for the actual calendar update.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation explicitly allows non-organizer attendees to call it (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(...);` and the FORBIDDEN check permits `isAttendee`). However, the calendar update path builds the `EventManager` with the calling user (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });`) and then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` where `evt.organizer` is derived from the booking organizer (`booking.userPrimaryEmail`/`organizer.email`). This is a concrete mismatch in the diff: if an attendee (not the organizer) triggers the mutation, the code will attempt calendar syncing using the attendee’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which is likely incorrect for updating the organizer-owned calendar event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `addGuestsHandler` is a single ~150-line function mixing auth, Prisma queries, `CalendarEvent` construction, calendar sync, and email dispatch — worth decomposing for readability/testability, consistent with other patterns in the router.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `addGuestsHandler` as a long, multi-responsibility function (~170 lines) that combines authorization checks, Prisma reads/writes, CalendarEvent assembly, calendar sync, and email sending. While this is verifiably true from the diff, it is a maintainability/readability suggestion rather than a bug, security issue, correctness problem, or clear defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx`) re-declares its own Zod validation schema instead of importing `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` from `addGuests.schema.ts`; the two can silently drift (e.g., server schema doesn't currently enforce uniqueness at all).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the client defines its own `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` as `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` (including a uniqueness refine), while the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` is a different shape (`{ bookingId: number, guests: string[] }`) and does not enforce uniqueness at the schema level. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable duplication/drift: the same-named “schema” differs across client/server, and the client’s extra constraint (uniqueness) is not guaranteed by the server schema.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`/`OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` template classes (`packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`) duplicate near-identical `getNodeMailerPayload` bodies from their `*-scheduled-email.ts` counterparts; could share more via the parent class.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two new template classes (`packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) that override `getNodeMailerPayload()`, but the proposed finding is a maintainability/DRY refactor suggestion rather than a verifiable defect. Also, the diff does not include the contents of the `*-scheduled-email.ts` counterparts, so the claim that these bodies are “near-identical” cannot be directly verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `getTranslation` is invoked per-attendee inside `Promise.all` without any caching, so bookings with many attendees/guests incur N sequential-per-item i18n loads.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `getTranslation` is called inside `bookingAttendees.attendees.map(async ...)`, so there are potentially N calls (one per attendee). However, these calls are executed concurrently via `Promise.all`, not sequentially as the finding claims. Also, the diff does not show whether `getTranslation` itself caches translations internally, so the “without any caching” assertion is not verifiable from this change alone. At most, it’s a speculative performance concern, not a clearly provable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isTeamAdmin`/`isTeamOwner` are awaited sequentially rather than via `Promise.all`, adding avoidable latency to every call.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which awaits the two async checks sequentially. If these checks are independent (likely DB queries), they could be run in parallel via `Promise.all`, so the current code adds avoidable latency on every call path that evaluates both checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded `name: ""` for new guest attendee records — fine for now since the UI only collects emails, but worth a comment noting the limitation for future readers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `name: ""` when creating new attendee records in `addGuests.handler.ts` (`guestsFullDetails`). However, this is an intentional consequence of the UI only collecting emails (no name field) and there’s no verifiable defect shown in the diff (e.g., no validation/schema in the diff requiring non-empty names, no failing usage). The proposed finding is essentially a documentation/style suggestion (“worth a comment”), not a clear bug/security/correctness problem proven by the changes.
